title: SWE-RL: Advancing LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning on Open Software Evolution
data_curation: Training data is sourced from open GitHub software evolution: all GitHub events from GH Archive (Jan 2015-Aug 2024) plus git clones of 4.6M repositories. These are aggregated into 24M merged-PR instances, reconstructing issue discussions, merge-base code contents, intermediate commits, and a cumulative oracle patch; all SWE-bench repositories are excluded to prevent contamination. To counter a learned bias of editing every shown file, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct predicts relevant-but-unmodified files to add as context. Filtering removes bot PRs (keywords like 'dependabot', 'renovate', 'bump', 'automerge'), empty or huge-change PRs, and applies CodeLlama hunk filters (e.g. lock-file-only changes), yielding ~11M unique PRs. Heuristics then select 273k high-quality seeds (linked issue describing a bug fix, programming-file changes) as the RL dataset. The SFT baseline instead uses Magicoder/OSS-Instruct-style synthetic data generated by Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, mixed with Llama 3 coding/general SFT data (2B tokens).
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. The RL model is trained in a single GRPO stage directly on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct (1,600 steps, 16k context, global batch 512 with 16 rollouts per each of 32 problems, Adam, ~32 wall-time hours on 512 H100 GPUs); the SFT baseline (Llama3-SWE-SFT-70B, 2B tokens, 16k context) is a separate comparison model rather than a warmup stage for RL.
method: SWE-RL is the first RL method for real-world software engineering using rule-based rewards over software-evolution (PR) data, avoiding costly execution feedback. Given an issue plus full file contents, the policy LLM reasons in an inner-monologue then emits search/replace edits; generations are converted to a unified patch. The reward is R(o) = -1 for malformed output, otherwise compare(patch_pred, patch_gt) via Python's difflib.SequenceMatcher, a continuous 0-1 sequence-similarity score. Policy optimization uses GRPO: G=16 rollouts per prompt, group-normalized advantages A_i = (r_i - mean)/std, a clipped importance-sampling ratio with epsilon, and a KL penalty beta * D_KL(pi_theta || pi_ref) to a reference policy. Conditioning on complete files implicitly forces fault localization before repair. A continuous-reward ablation beats a discrete exact-match reward (repair 34.8 vs 29.0) because real patches rarely match exactly. Inference uses the Agentless Mini scaffold (file localization, repair, reproduction/regression tests, CodeT dual-execution reranking).
eval_metrics: Evaluation centers on SWE-bench Verified (500 human-verified GitHub issues), metric pass@1 with 500 repair samples at temperature 1.0 and top-30 reproduction tests for reranking. Llama3-SWE-RL-70B scores 41.0%, SOTA among <100B models and comparable to GPT-4o+Agentless (38.8%); it beats the SFT baseline (36.2%). Repair-only with oracle files: 34.8 vs 29.6 (SFT) vs 5.4 (base greedy); format accuracy 95.6%. Generalization is probed on five OOD benchmarks (zero-shot greedy): HumanEval+ 79.9 (vs 76.2 base), BigCodeBench-Hard (I)/(C) 28.4/29.1, CRUXEval-I/O 71.6/75.5 (vs 60.5/61.9), MATH-strict 73.7 (vs 63.2; SFT drops to 54.0), MMLU 86.82. Scaling: repair samples 20->160 lift 33.6->40.0 then plateau; test samples 1->20 lift 38.8->41.0. Eval Arena thresholds give 0.05-level significance.
key_results: Llama3-SWE-RL-70B reaches 41.0% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, SOTA for <100B models and comparable to GPT-4o, vs 36.2% for the SFT baseline. Repair-only with oracle files: 34.8 vs 29.6 (SFT) vs 5.4 (base Llama-3.3-70B). OOD generalization: MATH-strict 73.7 vs 63.2 base; CRUXEval-I 71.6 vs 60.5 base.
evolution_note: Builds on DeepSeek-R1's rule-based-reward RL for math/competitive-code reasoning, extending it to real-world software engineering via PR-level software-evolution data and GRPO, without the proprietary-teacher distillation used by Lingma-SWE-GPT/SWE-Gym/SWE-Fixer. It is the first to show RL on SE artifacts yields emergent 'aha-moment' reasoning that generalizes to OOD math/code tasks, motivating RL over real-world code artifacts as a new post-training direction for 2025.
